title: Horses and Men: Tales, long and short, from our American life
summary: "Horses and Men: Tales, long and short, from our American life" by Sherwood Anderson is a short story collection published in 1923. Anderson's third collection following the acclaimed "Winesburg, Ohio," this volume presents nine stories exploring American life. The book includes tales previously published in magazines like The Dial and Harper's, alongside original works drawn from Anderson's unpublished novel manuscripts. Dedicated to Theodore Dreiser, the collection offers Anderson's distinctive portraits of American characters and experiences, from foolish youth to troubled spirits navigating modern life.
